clue.text: Leave message outside? Almost!

indicators.note: the message is placed outside, wrapping round the word for leave

parts.note: a note is a short written message
to quit is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a farewell note left outside nearly counts as a proper goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nearly but not fully achieved falls just short, an idiom meaning very close.

clue.text: We settled in a cosy place, making it most up-to date

indicators.note: the pronoun settles inside the snug home word

parts.note: a nest is a snug home

explanation.surface: A couple settle into a snug home and make it as modern as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent or latest, superlative of new.

clue.text: Three times as much rubbish covering lake

indicators.note: the rubbish word covers, so wraps around, the lake letter

parts.note: tripe means nonsense, rubbish
L is a map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Three times as much litter is now covering the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Threefold, multiplied by three.

clue.text: Fixed nut that is loose

indicators.note: fixed can mean rigged or tampered with, so the letters are altered

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A mechanic finds the nut supposed to be fixed has come loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' is the verb, to set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a knot is to undo or unfasten it.

clue.text: TV programme that requested after dining out

explanation.surface: A diner asks for a TV show after eating out.
explanation.walkthrough: This was a long-running British TV police drama; 'the Old Bill' is also slang for police.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running British police drama series shared its title with the restaurant tab diners ask for.

clue.text: Flatten a gourd

explanation.surface: An instruction to crush a vegetable flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush something is to make it flat; a marrow-like vegetable of the gourd family has the same name.

clue.text: Dance badly in middle of street after court appearance?

indicators.note: the inner construction comes after the court word

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a courtyard

indicators.note: the word for badly goes inside the centre letters of street
the middle of a word is its central letters

parts.note: ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Someone dances badly in the street after appearing in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' keeps the centre pair of 'street'; 'in' puts the badly word inside them. 'appearance?' only completes the courtroom picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrille is a square dance for four couples.

clue.text: Where one may come down and take off clothes to music

indicators.note: stripping is done to music, so the clothes word follows

parts.note: an air is a tune, music
to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A striptease performer undresses to music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come down' and 'take off' look like undressing but also describe landing and take-off by aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing strip for light aircraft, where planes land.

clue.text: Place for cool cats: The Ball and Socket

explanation.surface: A trendy club called The Ball and Socket.
explanation.definitionFit: A trendy nightspot for fashionable people, and the ball-and-socket articulation of the pelvis and thigh bone.

clue.text: Instrument that's right for a painter

parts.note: a whistle is a small musical instrument

explanation.surface: Someone picks out the perfect musical instrument to give an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: James McNeill Whistler was the American-born painter famous for the portrait of his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: James McNeill Whistler was a celebrated nineteenth-century artist.

clue.text: Governor finding gin on sale — 50% off!

indicators.note: the snare word is placed on, that is after, the halved word
half the letters of sale are knocked off, keeping its first half

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for catching animals

explanation.surface: A governor spots bottles of gin reduced to half price in a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like the drink but is the old word for an animal snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia.

clue.text: Husband of Ruth in the Bible and leading character in Dickens

definitions.text: Husband of Ruth in the Bible

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the pen name

parts.note: Boz was Charles Dickens's pen name
A is the first letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A biblical figure and a lead part in a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading character' looks like a hero but is A, the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Ruth, the landowner Boaz marries the widow Ruth.

clue.text: Order or lines of battle

indicators.note: to order is to rearrange, so these letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A commander debates the ordering or the lines of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' rearranges the letters of OR LINES OF. Solferino (1859) was a bloody battle of Italian unification that inspired the founding of the Red Cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Solferino was an 1859 engagement between French-Sardinian and Austrian armies.

clue.text: Nine-to five, say, in corporation

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the word corporation, read straight through

explanation.surface: Office workers in a big company keep nine-to-five hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nine-to five' looks like working hours, but read as 9:5 it is a proportion between two numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine to five, written 9:5, is a proportion comparing two quantities.

clue.text: Work on a large stone

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A stonemason sets to work on a big block.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone.

clue.text: Game of hockey's first introduced to rural workers

indicators.note: the letter is introduced into the workers word, going inside it

parts.note: peasants are farm labourers

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word hockey

explanation.surface: Farm labourers are introduced to the game of hockey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like a sport, but means birds shot for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Game birds hunted for sport and food.

clue.text: A very large number suffering in Jerusalem

indicators.note: the word for suffering goes inside the name for Jerusalem

parts.note: Zion is a poetic name for Jerusalem
ill means unwell, suffering

explanation.surface: A huge number of people are suffering in Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal, indefinite but enormous quantity, like a gazillion.

clue.text: Gone east, gone west that was long ago

indicators.note: gone west means wrecked or destroyed, so the letters are broken up

explanation.surface: Something that went east and then went west happened long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone west' is an idiom for ruined, so it rearranges GONE EAST.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric era of stone tools was a very ancient period.

clue.text: Measure of particular importance

parts.note: specific means particular
gravity means seriousness, importance

explanation.surface: A measure of particular importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Relative density, a physical quantity comparing a substance with water.

clue.text: Hats for those who get ahead?

explanation.surface: Hats suit people who come out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Top hats are formal tall headwear; jokingly, beheaders are people who take off tops, and getting a head is the pun.

clue.text: Silly piano

explanation.surface: A silly pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft means foolish; piano in music means quiet, gentle.

clue.text: Info about head of loch or valley

indicators.note: the information word wraps around the letter taken from loch

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks for information about the top of a Scottish loch or its valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: See
Excursions made by family members on first of June

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the month

parts.note: aunts are relatives

explanation.surface: Relatives make trips at the start of June.
explanation.definitionFit: Short pleasure trips.

clue.text: Good news -usual odds ignored in port

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Good news: the usual odds are ignored at the port.
explanation.walkthrough: Odessa is a Black Sea port in Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea seaport.

clue.text: Nothing to report in police stations

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Officers say there is nothing to report at the police stations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The nick' is British slang for a police station (or prison).
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a lock-up or police station is called the nick.

clue.text: Model for a grand painter

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are reshaped into the name

explanation.surface: Someone sits as an artist's model for a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' is slang for a thousand pounds, but here it is just fodder. Jean-Honoré Fragonard was an eighteenth-century French Rococo artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Honoré Fragonard was a French Rococo artist, known for The Swing.

clue.text: Plant kiss on cheek? Love comes first!

indicators.note: the love letter is placed first in the line
the kiss is placed on the cheek, so the cheek word follows it

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis
lip means cheek, impudence

explanation.surface: A kiss on the cheek, with love first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheek' looks like the face but means impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a primrose-family wildflower.

clue.text: Fundamentally affectionate if given gold first

indicators.note: the metal symbol is told to come first, before the word for affectionate

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
fond means loving, affectionate

explanation.surface: Someone becomes much fonder once gold is offered first.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means at bottom, basically, used in English too.

clue.text: Bad lad cares about region

indicators.note: the caring word goes around the scrambled lad

parts.note: to mind is to care, so minds means cares

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naughty boy worries about where he lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cares' looks like a noun but is a verb; 'Bad' jumbles the boy's letters. The Midlands is the central region of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Midlands are the central counties of England, an area of the country.

clue.text: One hundred plunges in river seems extreme. It's too much!

indicators.note: the hundred dives into the river, so it goes inside

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A hundred people diving into a river seems an extreme stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England. 'extreme' takes the first and last letters of 'seems', S and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Surplus beyond what is needed is an overabundance.

clue.text: Soap is my substitute for drinking-parties

indicators.note: a substitute swaps things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone swaps soap for drink at parties.
explanation.walkthrough: In ancient Greece a symposium was a convivial drinking session with talk.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece these were convivial gatherings for wine and conversation.
